caseStudy.label: Case study
caseStudy.heading: What maintaining looks like
caseStudy.intro: The strongest proof isn't a repo — it's what happens when other people start depending on one. fiscal-rs began as a port I wrote alone; today the community extends it and my job is to hold the line.
caseStudy.beat1Text: Community contributions across MDF-e, CT-e and NFS-e — reviewed, tested locally and shipped in coordinated crates.io releases.
caseStudy.beat2Text: Review blocked a symlink attack via predictable temp dirs and a panic on legacy A1 certificates — both reproduced before requesting changes.
caseStudy.beat3Text: The npm package had shipped broken since 0.7.0 and nobody noticed — there was no real consumer. I installed it, found it, fixed it, and moved publishing to OIDC with signed SLSA provenance.
caseStudy.closing: Every claim above is public — the pull requests, the releases, the provenance log.
